story.title: Nobody Would Use Him
story.text: Late in the Shang dynasty, an able old man with white hair still had no one to serve.
story.narration: Late in the Shang dynasty there lived an able old man named Jiang Ziya. His hair had turned white, yet nobody would give him a post, and he had to get by on his own.

story.title: The Willing One
story.text: At the Wei River he fished with a straight hook, no bait, three feet above the water.
story.narration: He fished in the Wei River. Legend says his hook was straight, with no bait, and it hung three feet above the water. People laughed at him, and he said: “The willing one will come.” Later storytellers turned it into the saying “Grand Duke Jiang fishes — the willing one takes the hook.”

keyMoment.question: Why use a straight hook and no bait?

options.text: He was afraid of hurting the small fish
The one he was fishing for was not a fish
He did not know how to bend a hook

keyMoment.reveal: His hook was straight because he was waiting for someone who would come by choice.

misconceptions: A straight hook only means poor skill — bend it and the fish will come
If nobody comes, you should move on; waiting is a waste of time

quiz.question: How did Jiang Ziya fish in the Wei River?
options: With a straight hook and no bait
With a bent hook and tasty bait
With a big net instead of a rod
quiz.explanation: Legend says his hook was straight, with no bait, hanging three feet above the water — he was not fishing for fish.

quiz.question: In “the willing one takes the hook”, who is the willing one?
options: Someone who comes of his own accord
A fish that wants to bite
A customer who wants to buy fish
quiz.explanation: He was waiting for someone who would come by choice — and in the end King Wen came himself.

quiz.question: You want a big fish, but small fish keep biting. What do you do?
options: Let them go and keep waiting for the big one
Catch a basket of small fish first
Keep every small fish, let none go
quiz.explanation: The small fish were not what he wanted. He did not change his mind for them, and so he met the one worth waiting for.

temptations.line: A bent hook catches nothing but fish.
The one I am fishing for is not a fish.
Move somewhere else, and the one I wait for will not find me here.

lines: Not yet — the fish have not come.
There are fish down there. I do not watch them.
Whoever is willing will come on his own.
